title: Systems without a sufficient local state are out of scope

statements.text: The theorem is proved for local classical systems and applies to any theory that supplies a dynamically sufficient local state. A theory in which a subsystem's evolution depends on correlations with its exterior not represented in its local state, as with entangled parts, lies outside its scope.
statements.conditions: A consciousness attribution invoking such a theory would have to specify how the historical information is carried and how it bears on subsequent evolution.

standing.reason: A limit the paper states: it does not extend the theorem to such theories.

sources.quote: A physical theory that does not have a dynamically sufficient local state — for example, one in which a subsystem's evolution depends on correlations with its exterior that are not represented in its local state — lies outside the present scope
